newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Internal debt crippling Yugo economy - Institute.
newsitem.headline: Internal debt crippling Yugo economy - Institute.

text.p: Yugoslavia's massive internal debt is the main obstacle to improving the country's deep structural and financial problems, and only debt for equity swaps may provide a way out, economists said on Tuesday.

Companies owe commercial banks a total of 33 billion dinars (10 billion German marks), 23 billion dinars of which are long-term debts and the remainder are short-term, the Institute of Economic Sciences (IEN) said in its latest monthly report.
"Yugoslav companies will never be able to pay back these long-term debts, while short-term ones will have to be revolved due to negative cash-flow," Jovan Rankovic of the IEN told a news conference.
This could last indefinitely without substantial foreign help, another IEN economist Stojan Stamenkovic said.
"I am afraid there is no way out for the Yugoslav economy if current situation persists. It is a vicious circle with no remedy in sight," Stamenkovic told Reuters.
Around 75 percent of the long term debt is made up of foreign credits to local companies. Those companies now owe local banks who acted as guarantors for the foreign loans.
But because huge amounts of claims are unrecoverable, banks are unable to meet their own liabilities.
"This means that foreigners in effect own indebted Yugoslav banks and companies," Rankovic said.
"Foreign creditors will not be able to collect the debt for at least next 20 years. That is why we at IEN think it is in their interest to swap debt for equity, " he said.
Rankovic cautioned that Yugoslav industry uses only 35 percent of its total capacity.

"This makes our companies unprofitable. They are not able to service their debts or to maintain liquidity needed for the current volume of activity, let alone create fresh money for investment purposes," he said.
($1 = 1.5100 German marks) -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
